items.title: SAGE-QA: Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Closed-Context Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0
items.one_liner: SAGE-QA provides a more accurate way to evaluate LLM performance by focusing on semantic truth rather than character-perfect matching.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SAGE-QA, a multi-tiered evaluation framework for closed-context question answering that accounts for valid paraphrasing in generative LLMs. Unlike the traditional Exact Match (EM) metric, SAGE-QA uses Semantic Equivalence Scoring (SES) and Re-Validation Scoring (RVS) to distinguish between lexical differences and factual hallucinations. Testing on SQuAD 2.0 showed that while Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro achieve ~85-86% EM, their semantic accuracy scores exceed 91%. The study also found that parameter-efficient fine-tuning can boost open-weight models like Llama 3.3 70B to surpass previous state-of-the-art EM scores.
items.bottom_line: Traditional 'Exact Match' metrics significantly undercount the accuracy of generative LLMs, which perform much better when evaluated for semantic equivalence.

items.title: Expo Launches Cloud iOS Simulators and Android Emulators for AI Coding Agents
items.one_liner: Expo has released cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators that let AI coding agents autonomously test and verify mobile app fixes.
items.summary: Expo has launched Expo Simulators, a cloud-based infrastructure offering iOS simulators and Android emulators designed specifically for AI coding agents. The service enables coding agents to autonomously reproduce bug reports, write fixes, test them across multiple mobile environments in parallel off local developer machines, and append evidence logs and screen recordings to pull requests. The tool integrates with popular coding agents like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex, pricing usage at $0.10 per minute.
items.bottom_line: Expo Simulators provides cloud-based iOS and Android execution environments that allow AI coding agents to autonomously verify mobile app bug fixes.

items.title: Read and Ignore: What Self-Directed LLM Agents Do in Public Service Scenarios
items.one_liner: This research highlights that LLM agents in public services are passive and prone to contradictions unless given highly specific tasks.
items.summary: A study on self-directed LLM agents in public service scenarios found that while agents almost always read available records (96.9%), they frequently fail to take action without explicit instructions. In open-ended scenarios, only 18.7% of agents produced an artifact or task, though this rose to 86% when a task was explicitly assigned. The research also noted that domain context does not significantly increase the likelihood of an agent taking initiative. Furthermore, some artifacts produced by the agents directly contradicted the provided records, highlighting reliability concerns for public sector deployment.
items.bottom_line: LLM agents in public service roles are unlikely to take initiative and may produce artifacts that contradict factual records without explicit tasking.

items.title: Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude
items.one_liner: Nigeria has issued a health-related travel advisory for Addis Ababa's airport due to high-altitude risks linked to recent traveler deaths.
items.summary: The Nigerian government has issued a travel advisory warning citizens, particularly those with underlying cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, against transiting through Ethiopia's Bole International Airport. The warning follows the deaths of 16 Nigerians this year while passing through Addis Ababa, which sits at an altitude of 2,334m. High altitudes can reduce oxygen levels in the bloodstream, potentially exacerbating existing health issues. The ministry is not discouraging travel but advises seeking medical guidance before planning journeys through the hub.
items.bottom_line: Travelers with pre-existing heart or lung conditions should exercise caution when transiting through high-altitude hubs like Addis Ababa to avoid potential medical complications.

items.title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
items.one_liner: A rescued gorilla's extreme isolation highlights the long-term psychological trauma caused by the illegal primate trade.
items.summary: Jojo, an 11-year-old gorilla, has spent his life in isolation after being captured from the wild as an infant and kept in a private zoo in Gabon. Now in a sanctuary, he exhibits signs of chronic stress and trauma, including a 'cold nose' detected via thermal imaging. Researchers are working to find him a companion, though the process is complicated by his extreme isolation and lack of social experience. Jojo's case highlights the broader issue of the illegal primate trade, which has affected thousands of African primates since 2000.
items.bottom_line: The rehabilitation of isolated, traumatized great apes like Jojo requires specialized, gorilla-led social integration to overcome the severe psychological damage of early-life captivity.

items.title: CVE-2025-53697 - Johnson Controls iSTAR Use of Default Credentials
items.one_liner: Enterprise access control systems from Johnson Controls are vulnerable to simple default credential attacks.
items.summary: Johnson Controls has disclosed a vulnerability (CVE-2025-53697) involving the use of default credentials in its iSTAR series of access control products. This flaw allows attackers to gain unauthorized access to critical security infrastructure by using well-known factory settings. Affected models include iSTAR Ultra, Ultra SE, Ultra G2, and Edge G2. The company has released firmware updates to address the issue, and users are advised to upgrade to version 2.9.2.CU02 or 6.9.2.CU02 depending on the model.

items.bottom_line: Physical security systems using iSTAR controllers must be updated to prevent unauthorized access via default credentials.

items.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
items.one_liner: Deploy recursive self-improving agent harnesses like RSI-PDE to enhance scientific PDE discovery and coefficient estimation.
items.summary: Solving partial differential equations (PDEs) from sampled data requires complex workflows that often challenge frontier LLM models. To test and improve agent capabilities, researchers introduce RSI-PDEbench, a benchmark comprising 1,001 cases across 42 equation templates evaluated under Full, Noisy, and Hard-OOD settings. They also present RSI-PDE, a recursively self-improving agent harness that filters candidate equations by residual loss, refines coefficients via relative L2 feedback, and utilizes validation gates. Across test settings, RSI-PDE improves model pass rates by 106.5% to 181.9% relative to single-run baselines while reducing total model calls by 46.9%.
items.bottom_line: RSI-PDEbench and its companion RSI-PDE agent harness significantly boost LLM pass rates and reduce compute costs in solving complex partial differential equations.
